text:
Sam T.: Heads-up: discovered inconsistent labels between the top nav and the in-product docs panel. Nav shows `Help & Support`, panel header reads `Docs`, and some CTAs say `View docs`. Users get mixed signals.
Lina P.: Saw the same in user tests. They ask whether tutorials live in the panel or on the site. We should pick a single surface lexicon.
Nora (design): Proposal: nav label stays `Help`, panel header becomes `Console docs` and the panel intro line says `Guides & examples`. Keeps nav discoverable and panel contextual.
Mason C.: Analytics note: events currently are help_click, docs_panel_open, and external_docs_click. We need to map old events to new names so dashboards aren't broken. I can own the mapping.
docs-bot: Draft doc: https://docs.redwood.ai/console/lexicon-panel-recs (created by @Nora (design)) :spiral_notepad:
Sam T.: Accessibility nit: toggle button has no aria-expanded and screen readers just say "Button". Quick fix:
```
<button id=\"docs-toggle\" aria-expanded=\"false\" aria-label=\"Open console docs\">Docs</button>
```
Lina P.: Cross-link behavior: internal anchors currently open the external docs in a new tab and don't focus the panel. Users expect the panel to open to that section if available. Suggest deep-link to the panel with a fallback to new tab.
Mason C.: Implementation: intercept anchor clicks, if panel feature-flag and model present -> panel.open({anchor}). Emit event docs_deeplink with anchor and fallback flag. Add unit tests.
Nora (design): UX detail: when deep-linking into the panel, highlight target heading for 2.5s and show a small `Back to console` link at the top. I'll add mockups.
Sam T.: Microcopy: use `Open help` in nav, `Console docs` in header, and `View full docs` for external links. Short and consistent.
Lina P.: Let's have a tiny RFC with owners (copy, infra, analytics) by Thursday. I'll file it and tag @Mason @Nora.
Mason C.: I'll take analytics migration. Nora, can you update Figma and drop the accessibility checklist?
Nora (design): Will do. PR incoming later today.
Sam T.: Thanks all :thumbsup:
